claims.text: Approximately 4 at.% Cr should be added to HfZrTiTa0.53 during melting or processing.
Cr addition will induce a discrete Laves phase along the grain boundaries of the BCC matrix.
The Cr-induced Laves phase will interrupt a continuous brittle ordered phase or network in the baseline alloy.
The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy contains a predominantly continuous ordered phase that limits tensile ductility.
Baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of 786 MPa.
Baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
Baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 has a terminal strain of 13.5%.
The Cr-containing Laves phase will form a reticulated but dispersed boundary structure rather than a continuous brittle network.
Cr's atomic-size and mixing-enthalpy differences will promote partial phase separation into a minor Laves phase.
The Laves phase will act as a crack-arresting network and blunt crack propagation during tensile deformation.
Cr addition will provide solid-solution strengthening and precipitation hardening.
Cr addition will increase tensile ductility and uniform elongation by approximately 20–30% relative to baseline HfZrTiTa0.53.
The Cr-modified alloy's yield strength will remain within approximately 10% of the 786 MPa baseline.
Cr modification will not reduce impact-triggered chemical-energy release relative to the baseline.
The tensile prediction applies at room temperature under uniaxial loading at approximately 1×10^-3 s^-1.
Matched compression testing should also be conducted at room temperature at approximately 1×10^-3 s^-1.
Matched fragment-penetration tests can determine whether impact-triggered chemical-energy release is preserved.
The approximately 4 at.% Cr addition yields an HfZrTiTaCr0.5-type composition.
Identical processing of the baseline and Cr-modified alloys will ensure similar grain sizes and microstructural homogeneity.

The hypothesis is falsified by less than a statistically significant 20% increase in tensile ductility and uniform elongation, a yield-strength loss exceeding 10%, or any reduction in impact-triggered chemical-energy release.

contradictions.description: Approximately 4 at.% Cr is inconsistent with the stated HfZrTiTaCr0.5-type formula. Normalized HfZrTiTaCr0.5 contains about 11.1 at.% Cr and also changes Ta from Ta0.53 to Ta1.

The new Laves phase is alternately described as discrete and dispersed, reticulated, and a crack-arresting network. These descriptions leave unresolved whether it is discontinuous or itself forms a continuous network.
